landing.title: Understand Snipxn first, then enter your code notes workspace
landing.subtitle: Snipxn is a Markdown-first notes app for developers, focused on folder structure, snippet capture, multi-device sessions, and future offline sync. Browse the product first, then choose when to enter.
landing.hint: Opening the app no longer forces an immediate login redirect.
landing.featureNotesTitle: Notes and snippets stay in one working surface
landing.featureNotesBody: The middle column manages title, summary, and language tags while the right side keeps Markdown editing active, without forcing context switches.
landing.featureFoldersTitle: Folders, tags, and starred notes create stable structure
landing.featureFoldersBody: The left column keeps an explorer-like mental model that works well for coursework, experiments, and long-term snippet archiving.
landing.featureSessionTitle: Device-aware sessions are part of the product, not an afterthought
landing.featureSessionBody: Login, registration, refresh, and device management already align with the backend contract, so later sync work does not need a new entry flow.
landing.previewNoteBody: Keep APIs, page planning, and implementation phases in one place.
landing.previewSnippetBody: Capture deviceId, token refresh, and error handling details.
landing.previewCodeLine3: - refresh must carry the active device
landing.previewCodeLine4: - editor supports Markdown and image insertion
landing.storyTitle: Snipxn is not just a note page. It is a workflow built around how developers actually capture and continue work.
landing.storyBody: It turns the path of capture, organize, and continue into a stable three-step flow, whether the context is a graduation project, coursework, or a long-term snippet library.
landing.storyProblemBody: Many tools are good for long writing but awkward for dropping API details, code fragments, and half-formed implementation notes. Snipxn prioritizes quick capture before structure.
landing.storyFlowTitle: Then make organization the default path
landing.storyFlowBody: Folders, tags, starred notes, and scope switching stay in one workspace, so content accumulates through the interface itself instead of depending on discipline alone.
landing.storyShipTitle: Finish with something that feels product-grade
landing.storyShipBody: Device sessions, auth flow, workspace layout, and future sync direction are already part of the design, which makes the project easier to present as a real product instead of a static prototype.
landing.featureTitle: From the first screen to the editor, the page structure follows real developer usage patterns
landing.featureBody: The landing page does not stop at slogans. It previews how the workspace supports folder organization, note browsing, Markdown editing, and device-aware sessions.
landing.workflowTitle: Introduce, enter, and continue working. Those three steps need to feel natural.
landing.workflowBody: The landing page should help first-time visitors understand the product quickly, while giving returning users a near-frictionless way back into the workspace.
landing.workflowCaptureBody: Show the brand, product angle, and core interface first, then let people decide when to enter instead of dropping them straight into auth.
landing.workflowOrganizeBody: Use chapter-like content to explain editing, organization, session handling, and future sync direction instead of flattening everything into one feature list.
landing.workflowContinueBody: Whether the next step is sign in, registration, or returning to the workspace, the CTA appears in multiple places so users do not need to hunt for the next move.
landing.stackTitle: It works better when presented as a full system, not just a single page
landing.stackBody: For a graduation defense or product walkthrough, the value is not only the editor. It is the combination of backend contract, account-device flow, structured information, and a coherent demo path.
landing.quote: Turn fragmented development notes into a workspace you can keep reusing over time.
landing.stackItemApiBody: Login, registration, token refresh, and file upload naturally support discussion around API design, state handling, and failure paths.
landing.stackItemSessionBody: Current device context, refresh logic, and future sync direction make the system feel closer to a real product than a page with only an editor.
landing.stackItemEditorTitle: The editor is the center of gravity
landing.stackItemEditorBody: Markdown, image insertion, title and summary editing, language labels, and folder assignment all happen in one continuous surface.
landing.stackItemShowcaseTitle: The demo path is more complete
landing.stackItemShowcaseBody: From the landing page to auth, then into the workspace and settings, reviewers can see one connected product flow instead of isolated features.
landing.ctaTitle: You can enter Snipxn now instead of stopping at the intro page
landing.ctaBody: If this is your first visit, sign in and establish a device session. If this browser already has a session, jump straight back into the workspace and continue your code notes.
